description: Liquid-helium dewar: MWOL outer jacket, AERO liner, an LHE bath at 4 K with an NBTI coil submerged in it.
name: cryo_dewar_lhe
why: LHE boils at just 4.2 K and (like every cryogen in this framework) spawns at room temperature unless given an explicit cold props -- the bath here is placed at -269 C. NBTI only superconducts below its own critical temperature (Tc = 9.3 K), so the coil must stay fully immersed in the LHE pool at all times; a warm leak through the MWOL/AERO insulation boils the whole reservoir off in a few hundred frames and the coil goes resistive (modeled here simply as a normal conductor). Never route the coil or bath through bare METL -- use the AERO/MWOL jacket for every penetration.
